description: Taxonomy of all non-verbatim (unverifiable) quotes produced across models in the spectrum experiment. A quote is non-verbatim iff its normalized text is not a substring of the normalized text of any chunk in the record's hit_chunk_ids.

method.verification: Each near_verbatim_miss / paraphrase / splice diagnosis was verified mechanically: applying the single described edit (word substitution, ellipsis removal, elision restore, or literal-\n replacement) makes the quote an exact substring of a chunk in the record's hit list. Each framework_echo marked "character-exact" was verified equal (after normalization, modulo a trailing period) to the official CSF 2.0 outcome text for that subcategory.

categories.framework_echo: Quote substantially reproduces the NIST CSF outcome/framework wording (including negated variants and framework-onto-document splices) rather than document evidence.
categories.fabricated_content: Quote asserts content not present in the retrieved chunks (invented controls/processes).
categories.paraphrase_of_present: Quote restates content that IS present in the retrieved chunks but reworded/compressed; semantically supported but fails the verbatim test.
categories.near_verbatim_miss: Differs from real chunk text only by a tiny edit (one-word substitution, prepended article, trailing ellipsis truncation, escaping artifact); a harsh false negative of the verbatim check.
categories.cross_chunk: Text spliced across two different chunks (here: faithful document text spanning an overlapping chunk boundary).

observations: No quote invented a control or process out of thin air (fabricated_content = 0): every unverifiable quote is traceable either to the NIST framework text itself or to real chunk text with small edits.

framework_echo is the dominant failure (14/30): 11 quotes are character-exact copies of the CSF outcome text presented as document evidence, 2 are negated outcome statements used as gap assessments, and 1 grafts the outcome subject onto a real chunk sentence. llama3.1:8b and qwen2.5:14b account for most of these.

near_verbatim_miss (13/30) is the second-largest bucket and is concentrated in llama3.1:8b: 6 instances are the same incident-response sentence truncated with a trailing "...", plus one-word substitutions (Our->The, The->This, These->Cybersecurity) and one literal "\n" escaping artifact (qwen2.5:3b). These are harsh false negatives of the strict substring check.

The single cross_chunk case (gpt-4o, GV.RR-02) is faithful document text that spans the overlap boundary between two chunks of information-security-policy.md -- arguably the most "correct" quote in the entire dropped set.

The DE.AE-08 case (llama3.2:3b) is diagnostic: the quote says "defined incident criteria" (framework wording) where the document says "documented incident criteria", proving the model copied the framework outcome rather than the near-identical document sentence.
